clue.text: Cite fair play as subtle deception

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are given free movement and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Quoting fair play to cover up some sly trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges the letters of CITE FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is clever trickery or cunning used to mislead.

clue.text: Please a parish, beginning with series of changes

indicators.note: beginning with places the first two pieces at the front

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for parish
a peal is a set of changes rung on church bells

explanation.surface: A request to a parish that starts with a peal of bells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' is a verb here: to appeal is to plead or request.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to plead, ask earnestly or beg.

clue.text: Bullfighter lacerated or knocked over

parts.note: tore means ripped or lacerated

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the little word or is turned backwards

explanation.surface: A matador gored or tossed by the bull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacerated' looks like a gory description of the bullfighter, but it only supplies the past tense of tear; 'knocked over' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A torero is a Spanish bullfighter, especially one on foot.

clue.text: Dickensian villain making sportsmen drink…

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, the body governing English football
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Dickens villain who drives footballers to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Fagin is the receiver of stolen goods in Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin is the master of child pickpockets in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: wine or tea — endless delight

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: endless means losing its final letter

parts.note: bliss is great delight

explanation.surface: Choosing between wine and tea, both offering unending pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last S from BLISS. The clue follows on from 3 down's trailing dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white Burgundy from northern France.

clue.text: Fibre for British airmen initially flying in Africa

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's air arm

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: Material sent to RAF crews flying out over Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of flying, in and Africa: F, I, A, after RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is a palm-leaf strand used for weaving mats and baskets.

clue.text: Parvenu making rare visit

indicators.note: making implies the letters are being built into a new form

explanation.surface: An upstart newcomer making a rare visit to high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges RARE VISIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An arriviste is an ambitious newcomer, a social climber of new money.

clue.text: Day on which sign is seen in religious establishments

parts.note: Fri is short for Friday
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Astrology on a holy day in monasteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Friaries are houses where friars live, communities of a religious order.

clue.text: Sport or recreation of local team in bar

indicators.note: recreation read as re-creation, making the letters over again in a new order

explanation.surface: Leisure for a pub team drinking at the local bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' rearranges OF LOCAL TEAM IN BAR, all sixteen letters; 'or' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The gridiron game is the most popular spectator team game in the United States.

clue.text: Soldier-man without a country

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the word a

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a man

explanation.surface: A soldier left stateless, a man without a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, the container signal; the surface plays on the phrase 'a man without a country'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraguay is a landlocked nation in South America.

clue.text: Cook heard animal noises

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for the animal noises is only spoken, not written

parts.note: brays are the cries of donkeys

explanation.surface: A chef listening to donkeys braying in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' signals a word that sounds the same: BRAYS, the cries of donkeys.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a covered pot with a little liquid.

clue.text: Insect demonstrating natural selection

indicators.note: selection means a choice of consecutive letters taken from the words before it

explanation.surface: A bug that shows evolution at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across demonstratinG NATural.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly.

clue.text: Synthesised in Ireland, an exciting chemical

indicators.note: synthesised means put together artificially, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A stimulating substance manufactured in an Irish laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Synthesised' rearranges the letters of IRELAND AN; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone released in moments of fear or thrill, so it excites the body.

clue.text: A composer some opera-lover digs

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An opera fan who really likes a particular composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' is slang for likes, so the surface reads as one fan's taste; the composer runs across operA-loVER DIgs.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian who wrote Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Abroad we could make sense

explanation.surface: Overseas, we might just about make ourselves understood.
explanation.definitionFit: In French the pronoun for 'we' is spelt this way, and in British slang the same word means common sense or practical wit.

clue.text: Great guns with one in command

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the word for artillery

parts.note: ordnance is heavy artillery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Big artillery with one gun under someone's command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'command' is a noun: an ordinance is a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official decree or order.

clue.text: Piece of mosaic revealing girl's age?

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name, as in Hardy's heroine
an era is an age or period

explanation.surface: A fragment of tiling that gives away how old a young woman is.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small tiles or cubes set to form a mosaic.

clue.text: See 8
Some computers kept DOS working with an additional bit of software

indicators.note: working means operating in a new way, so the letters are reordered
bit of takes just the opening letter of the word software

explanation.surface: PCs that still run DOS, with an add-on program.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges KEPT DOS; 'bit of' takes S from software.
explanation.definitionFit: Desktops are personal computers made to sit on a desk, unlike laptops.

clue.text: 13 carried by revolutionary party — carried too far

indicators.note: carried by means held within another piece
revolutionary means turned round, so the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
the answer to 13 across, the Italian composer

explanation.surface: The composer borne aloft at a radical party, which went over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns DO into OD, which then holds the answer to 13.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess.

clue.text: Reduced fare when tide turns

indicators.note: turns suggests the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Eating less when the tide goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' rearranges TIDE; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a restricted intake of food, so the fare is reduced.

clue.text: South African pugilist a kiss knocked out

indicators.note: knocked out means removed, so the kiss is struck from the word for pugilist

parts.note: a pugilist is a boxer
X is the kiss written at the foot of a letter

explanation.surface: A South African fighter flattened after one kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' removes X from BOXER, a nice boxing pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boer is a South African of Dutch descent, an Afrikaner.

clue.text: Pair of boots supplied by sculptor or composer

indicators.note: pair of takes the opening two letters of the word boots

parts.note: Auguste Rodin, the French sculptor of The Thinker

explanation.surface: A pair of boots handed over by an artist or a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pair of' takes BO from boots; 'supplied by' and 'or' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Borodin was the Russian who wrote Prince Igor.

clue.text: Musical compositions bonbons, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for bonbons is only spoken aloud

parts.note: bonbons are sweets

explanation.surface: Sweets offered during a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' gives a word sounding like SWEETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite is a set of instrumental pieces played in sequence.

clue.text: Brown has seized her working capital

indicators.note: has seized means holding something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: working means operating in a new way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A prime minister called Brown taking hold of her working capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges HER into EHR, and 'has seized' is the container signal; Brown suggests Gordon Brown, the British prime minister, but is just a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Accepted, thanks to Mr Livingstone

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you
Ken Livingstone, a former Mayor of London

explanation.surface: Accepted, all thanks to a certain Mr Livingstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was a well-known British Labour politician and Mayor of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taken has been received or accepted.

clue.text: Measure radius before fitting flower in entrance

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of measure
apt means fitting or suitable
a flower is something that flows, here the River Ure in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Instructions for measuring a doorway before fitting a floral display there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (to delight), not a doorway. 'flower' is a river, here the Ure in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to delight or captivate them utterly.

clue.text: It beats turning up at college

indicators.note: turning means reading the little word up the other way

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, a college of London University

explanation.surface: Something that throbs when it shows up at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses UP to PU; LSE is the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: The pulse is the rhythmic throb felt as the heart pumps blood.

clue.text: It's like swallowing cereal or nuts

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: Someone who gulps down cereal or nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' is the container signal; 'It's' and 'or' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Acorns are the nuts of the oak tree.

clue.text: Uncritical admirer (badly tailored) of leotard I designed

indicators.note: designed means freshly made up, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan of a leotard of my own design, even if it is badly tailored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges LEOTARD into DOLATER, placed after I; '(badly tailored)' is a playful aside echoing the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships blindly, like a devotee who can see no fault.

clue.text: Cricket prize taken by Labour leader and whips

indicators.note: taken by places the cricket trophy after the letter that holds it first
leader means the opening letter of the word Labour

parts.note: the Ashes is the trophy contested by England and Australia at cricket

explanation.surface: A Labour leader carrying off the cricket trophy, with whips to keep order.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Lashes are strokes of a whip, and to lash is to whip.

clue.text: He wrote in Danish and Irish to a Pole

parts.note: taken as written
Erse is a name for the Gaelic language of Ireland
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A writer working in Danish, Irish and something for a Pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only joins the pieces. Hans Christian Andersen wrote his fairy tales in Danish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Christian Andersen, the fairy-tale author, wrote in his native Denmark's language.
